note: Lit displays and beloved digital places, for app UI, admin, dashboards and tools. Two waves taught the stocking. The first held machines and rooms and lost four of six to skeuomorphism: "way too extremely skeuomorphic", "objects that must be on screen". The second held what instruments print and lost three of six to indifference: "there's nothing interesting about this world". Neither was the answer. All sixteen three-star worlds in the interaction tier are a display or a beloved digital-era thing, and not one is a printed log or chart. A third reading of that list, that they all name a light source and an hour, turned out to be a feature of how they are described rather than what makes them work: half of them, the homepage neighborhood, the minihompy, the zine, the risograph, are not about light at all. The tier still converts best at 37% from the smallest pool of 43, which is why a wave here buys the most.

bar:
## The operate bar, which is not the bar for other modes

This world will be dealt to app UI, admin and tools. The register here is
earned familiarity rather than distinctiveness for its own sake: a fluent user
of Linear, Figma or Stripe should trust it on sight. That does not mean looking
like them.

**State is the whole job.** An operating surface is mostly states: selected,
disabled, pending, failed, stale, destructive, unavailable-because-of-something
else. Name a state vocabulary that reads without colour, because colour is the
first thing a theme, a projector or a colourblind user takes away. The rules
that travelled best across nine judged transfers were exactly this kind: state
as physical position, a printed mark, a struck line, a die-cut hole. Your
assigned instrument had to solve this under real consequence, so take its
answer rather than inventing one.

**It has to survive repetition.** This surface is used for hours, every day, by
someone who is not admiring it. A device that delights once and grates on the
fortieth pass is a persuade device in the wrong mode. Say what the world does
at rest, because at rest is where it mostly lives.

**Density is not the enemy.** Operating surfaces carry a lot and generous
emptiness often reads as an unfinished tool. Say how the world stays legible
when packed, and prefer rules, hairlines and grouping over space.

**Take the marking system, never the machine.** Your assigned tradition is
something an instrument prints or displays. Design from its graphic logic: its
legends, its scales, its state marks, its layout. Do not depict the instrument.
A wave stocked with machines produced worlds rejected as "way too extremely
skeuomorphic" and "way too heavily influenced by specific objects that must be
on screen", and a render model will happily add screws, bezels and brushed metal
to any of them.

This is not a ban on dimension. Spatial design works when it is a system: relief
where raised means actionable and inset means editable is spatial and carries
real meaning. What fails is a specific physical object that has to be drawn for
the world to exist.

**The other failure to avoid.** Do not author a contemporary product surface. A
neutral greyscale application, a soft-cornered card on a warm tint, a dark
developer console: the catalog holds all three, they are what a model produces
unprompted, and two were rejected as boring on exactly that ground.
